title: Roles and access restrictions
goal: Test object and row-level restrictions with negative cases without broadening permissions.
prerequisites: onec.p9; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.
outcomes: Actual input/output and exact own source identified; unperformed stages marked NOT RUN.
Accepted original preserved; rejection and its limits explained.
sections: A role permits object operations; data restrictions refine scope. A user allowed Alpha requests does not gainBeta access merely by knowing a key. Test lists, direct open and edits. Hidden buttons and editable client filters are not authorization enforcement.

Continue module 6 own roles: administrator reads/writes; the training reader reads and is denied a valid write. These are infobase roles, not Nexus accounts/RLS. Use an otherwise valid write so range validation is not mistaken for an authorization rejection.

Additional roles change effective permissions. Analyze the full set and context, not one role alone. Full rights can hide missing enforcement. Use separate synthetic least-privilege profiles and a positive control so a denial is not merely an inability to log in.

For advanced RLS in another copy restrict document Read with WHERE ДлительностьМинут <=30, matching the current schema. Do not load the historical Минуты fixture over learner work. A second broader role can widen access; inspect the complete role set.

Privileged execution can alter normal permission boundaries. Do not enable it merely to silence a read error; justify need and outputs. Even aggregates can disclose forbidden information. Agree on a minimal contract and test indirect routes as well as visible records.

The final 12 values yield 5 visible records:30, 15, 0, 20, 25, total 90. Compare SELECT ALLOWED with an unrestricted query in an admitted own module: one returns the subset; access to prohibited rows must reject. Separately the administrator sees 12/440.
Bind the matrix to the actual environment

Record build, profile, object, action, scope and expectation. TestAlpha, Beta, direct references, writes and aggregates in a suitable stand. Mark unavailable training checksNOTRUN. Logs contain no passwords or full user data; successful login is not a complete security audit.

Record permitted object reading, denied update,30/35 boundary and unchanged prior fields. Own synthetic profiles need no password/OS authentication for this exercise. If the edition lacks the mode, complete object-right checks and leave RLS explicitly NOT RUN.
